final_prompt:
I want a habit tracker for just me, as a local web app that runs in the browser. There are no accounts or login, and the data stays on this machine. This is an MVP: build the thinnest working slice, throwaway structure is fine, and don't write tests or abstractions.

Build it in a new folder, `habit-tracker`, inside the current working directory. Don't touch anything outside it. Use React + Vite with TypeScript (I prefer TypeScript), and store all data in the browser's localStorage. Run it locally with the Vite dev server.

Build only these features:
- [ ] Track multiple habits. I can add a habit by name.
- [ ] Daily check-off. I can mark each habit done or not done for today.
- [ ] Current streak shown for each habit.
- [ ] A simple 30-day history per habit, showing which of the last 30 days were checked.

Do not build reminders, a calendar view, or charts or stats beyond the 30-day history. Editing and deleting habits were not requested. Include them only if you judge a minimal version necessary, and tell me if you did.

Decide the look and feel yourself (styling, layout, naming) and note your choice in your final summary. Decide small edge cases yourself too, such as how streaks treat today when it isn't checked yet, and note them. Ask me only if something blocks you completely.

Verify by running the app, not just writing it. Start the dev server, then check this flow, using a browser tool if you have one:
1. Add 2 habits.
2. Check one off for today.
3. Reload the page.
4. Confirm the check and the streak are still there.
Report the commands you ran and what you observed. If the flow fails, fix the cause and rerun it.

You're done when that flow passes, the dev server starts cleanly with one command, and you've given me a short summary with the run command, your look-and-feel and edge-case choices, and anything extra you added.
